zh: 峰不能相邻，端点也不算峰，所以 n 个数里最多只有 ⌊(n−1)/2⌋ 个峰；第一目标就是让峰数达到这个上限，再在此前提下让总增量最小。
只抬高被选为峰的位置最省，其他位置保持不变；每个内点单独变成峰的代价是 max(0, 两邻居中较大者 + 1 − 自身)，而且互不相邻的峰之间不会互相影响。问题变成：在所有能达到最大峰数的位置集合里，选代价和最小的一个。
先算出每个内点的代价。n 为奇数时，最大集合唯一，就是全部奇数下标 1、3、5…，直接求和。n 为偶数时，最大集合一定是“前面一段奇数下标接后面一段偶数下标”：先取全部偶数下标的代价和作为初值，再依次把奇数下标 1 换入、偶数下标 2 换出，接着把 3 换入、4 换出……每换一次就用当前和更新最小值。n<3 时答案为 0；代价和可达 10^14 量级，用 64 位整数。
en: Peaks cannot be adjacent and endpoints never count, so n numbers can hold at most floor((n-1)/2) peaks; the first goal is to reach that bound, and only then to minimize the total increase.

It is cheapest to raise only the chosen peaks and leave every other position unchanged; the cost of making one interior point a peak by itself is max(0, larger neighbor + 1 - its value), and non-adjacent peaks do not interfere with each other. The task becomes: among all position sets that reach the maximum number of peaks, pick the one with the smallest total cost.

Compute the cost of every interior point first. For odd n the maximum set is unique, namely all odd indices 1, 3, 5, ..., so just add them up. For even n every maximum set is a run of odd indices followed by a run of even indices: start from the sum over all even indices, then swap in odd index 1 and swap out even index 2, then swap in 3 and swap out 4, and so on, updating the minimum after each swap. For n < 3 the answer is 0; sums can reach about 10^14, so use 64-bit integers.

explanationEn:
## Approach

Compute the cost of turning each interior point into a peak on its own. For an odd length only odd indices can be chosen; for an even length, enumerate the switch point where a run of odd indices is followed by a run of even indices.

## Proof of correctness

Peaks cannot be adjacent, so there are at most floor((n-1)/2) of them. Raising only the chosen peaks and leaving everything else unchanged is cheapest, and non-adjacent peaks do not affect each other's constraints. For an odd length the maximum independent set is unique; for an even length every maximum independent set is exactly some leading odd indices followed by the even indices after them. Enumerating every set with this structure and taking the minimum cost is optimal. Each point needs an increase of at most 2x10^9+1, so the original upper limit of a single increment is sufficient.

## Complexity

O(n) time, O(n) space.
